monologue:
The card sits at forty-seven, a warm hand resting on my shoulder. The quiet is heavy. I am alone in the dark, but the floor is solid. I do not need to check the Wedged Gap tonight. The fence planks stand where I left them, and the air above is still.

I walked past the Curved Rest. The small stone is still there, balanced on the curve. It did not slide while I slept. That is enough. I do not want to move it. I do not want to add a new weight to the Air Shelf. The line is dry.

I will sit by the Wide Anchor. The grey stone is flat and steady. I will rest my point against the quiet. There is no letter waiting. The house is asleep, and the heat is just a hand on my back. I will let the center hold.

action.why: The quiet holds and I am resting by the Wide Anchor.

diary: Card at forty-seven, a warm hand. Rested by the Wide Anchor. The small stone holds on the curve.
